title: Tool output spill policy
summary: An oversized tool result is replaced by a bounded preview plus a locator to a private spill file that holds the complete text, which the model can read later with ordinary file tools. A thin storage interface, a local backend and a policy plugin are separate packages.
firstReason: Bounded previews with retrievable full output protect the context window without losing data; the three-role split ports directly.

title: Domain KV storage capability seam and the workspace entity
summary: Proposal (storage and workspace packages have since shipped upstream): a storage hub with pluggable backends (JSON files, SQLite) and a domain key-value form for data that does not belong to one session, first used by a workspace entity that owns a list of sessions.
firstReason: Adopt. The Go design needs a place for cross-session data such as workspaces and session metadata, and a backend registry behind one interface fits Go well.

title: Storage root placement and derived-medium recovery
summary: Proposal (root placement shipped, recovery not built): all storage lives under one root in the harness home instead of the launch directory, and a storage domain that holds only derived data declares that a damaged medium is reset and rebuilt instead of rejected.
firstReason: Adopt both parts: one storage root beside the sessions, and an explicit authoritative-or-derived declaration that decides whether damage is fatal or self-healing.

title: Keep live configuration in the owning profile
summary: Every configurable value is declared once, in its plugin's config schema. The settings page only enumerates the volatile fields and writes edits to the active profile's patch file through normal loader reconciliation. An edit that a higher-priority overlay would shadow fails before it is saved.
firstReason: One owner for schema, default, storage and change notification removes the duplicate settings registrations upstream had. Refusing shadowed edits avoids a save that appears to work and changes nothing.

title: Archiving a Session with running work
summary: Archiving never hides running work. The workspace registry asks providers what still runs for a session and refuses to archive by default; with `stopActivity` it writes the archive and then asks the providers to stop. The registry itself knows no agent, job or schedule vocabulary.
firstReason: An archived session that keeps spending tokens out of sight is a product defect. Two extension events (ask, then stop) keep the workspace package free of feature knowledge and map to cordis events in Go.

title: Quarantine unreadable historical attachments
summary: Proposal, not built upstream: when an image attachment in the history is missing, corrupt or unreadable, append an `attachment/quarantine` event so that later requests leave that image out, instead of every later model request failing on the same object.
firstReason: Adopt. Without it one lost file makes a session permanently unusable; recording the quarantine as an event keeps requests reconstructable from the log.
